land.text: the Electorate of Bavaria, raised to a kingdom on 1 January 1806

predecessors.note: The Bavaria page's infobox also lists the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg and the Imperial County of Ortenburg as predecessors; both had passed to the electorate by 1806 (Würzburg: Recess of 1803, then exchanged away in 1805).

land.text: the People's State of Bavaria, which 'became' the former kingdom and entered the Weimar Republic as a state

successors.note: The kingdom was a federated state of the German Empire from 18 January 1871 and ended with the Anif declaration of 12 November 1918 (Eisner's government treated it as Ludwig III's abdication; 'the former Kingdom of Bavaria became the People's State of Bavaria'). The German Empire was its overlord, not its successor, so it is no longer listed here (fx-46 R122, was the 1871 dissolve into german-empire); the hierarchy.csv row Bavaria -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. Cliopatria's last Bavaria shape is 1870.

rulers.name: Ludwig II
rulers.note: The reign runs past the map's 1871 end of the state.

correction.text: the 1806 shape plus the former Prince-Bishopric of Bamberg, Bavarian since the 1802-03 occupation and Recess

keyframe_review.note: 84,896 km2 against the infobox 75,865 km2 (1910; the source list says 1900), ratio 1.12. The shape has Tyrol, Vorarlberg and Augsburg (Pressburg page) but not Bamberg: the German mediatisation page says Bavaria 'occupied Bamberg and Würzburg in August 1802' and received Bamberg under the Recess of 25 Feb 1803, so Bamberg belongs inside the 1806 state; Cliopatria adds it only in 1807 (3 of 12 cells within 30 km of Bamberg in 1806, 12 of 12 from 1807). Würzburg is rightly absent (given up in 1805, Würzburg page).

90,319 km2 against 75,865 km2 (ratio 1.19, within the factor of two; the shape still holds Tyrol, Vorarlberg and the Trentino, which the 1910 infobox figure does not). Includes Bamberg, Tyrol and Augsburg; no Salzburg and no Bayreuth (Hof absent), which matches the Bayreuth page: Prussia ceded it in 1807, France offered it for sale in 1808 and it 'changed owners in 1810'. No opened page covers Ansbach: unverified: page budget.

correction.text: all of Bavaria including Tyrol and the Trentino, with Tyrol contested by the rebels from April to 1 November 1809; applies to 1809 only

keyframe_review.note: The shape (1809-1810) drops about 18 cells of Tyrol and the Trentino for two years. The Tyrolean page: the rebellion broke out 12-13 March 1809, Austria declared war on 9 April and 'the last rebel troops were defeated at the Fourth Battle of Bergisel on 1 November'; Bavaria ceded the Trentino and southern Tyrol only on 28 February 1810. So for 1809 the state is the full 1807 shape with Tyrol contested (ledger contest_start 1809/4, contest_end 1809/11); the shape applies to 1809 only, and 1810 is the new keyframe kingdom-of-bavaria_1810.

correction.text: the 1811 shape plus the Duchy of Salzburg, united with Bavaria 1810-1816

keyframe_review.note: 82,909 km2 (ratio 1.09). The shape rightly lacks the Trentino and Bolzano (ceded to Italy on 28 February 1810, Tyrolean page) and adds Hof and the Bayreuth land (1810, Bayreuth page). Regensburg, incorporated on 22 May 1810 (Regensburg page), is already inside every shape from 1806 (an enclave smaller than the 253 km2 cell). It never contains Salzburg (1 of 26 Salzburg cells in every shape), although the Bavaria page says 'Salzburg (1810-1816) [was] temporarily united with Bavaria' and the Munich treaty page has Bavaria ceding 'the duchy of Salzburg' in 1816. Add Salzburg for 1811-1813.

correction.text: the 1814 shape plus the Duchy of Salzburg, still Bavarian until the Treaty of Munich of 14 April 1816

keyframe_review.note: 89,087 km2 (ratio 1.17). Right to hold Tyrol and Vorarlberg through 1814 ('Tyrol (1806-1814)') and to add Würzburg and Aschaffenburg in the year of the treaty of June 1814 (Würzburg page: Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814; Bavaria page: Bavaria 'received Aschaffenburg and Würzburg'). Salzburg is again missing although Bavarian until 1816.

correction.text: the 1815 shape plus the Duchy of Salzburg; applies to 1815 only, 1816-1819 is kingdom-of-bavaria_1816

keyframe_review.note: 71,407 km2 (ratio 0.94). Tyrol and Vorarlberg are correctly gone (ceded 1814); Salzburg is missing for 1815 (Bavarian until the 14 April 1816 treaty) and the Palatinate is missing for 1816-1819, although the Munich treaty page gives Bavaria 'the former French arrondissements of Kaiserslautern, Speyer, and Zweibrücken' and other left-bank cantons. The shape applies to 1815 plus Salzburg; from 1816 use the new keyframe kingdom-of-bavaria_1816.

76,347 km2 (ratio 1.01). The first shape with the Palatinate (left bank, Treaty of Munich 14 April 1816) and the right-bank bailiwicks; it also holds the Alzenau-Miltenberg land that the treaty page says Austria would help Bavaria obtain from Hesse-Darmstadt and Baden (transfer date not on the page). Two Rhön/Coburg-border cells (10.2-10.93E, 50.28-50.47N) flicker between the 1820, 1828, 1836 and 1840 shapes; no opened page explains them (unverified: page budget).

76,568 km2 against 75,865 km2 (ratio 1.01). No territorial change of the kingdom is recorded on the Bavaria page between 1816 and 1866; differences from the neighbouring shapes are at the one-or-two-cell level (unverified: page budget).

76,590 km2 against 75,865 km2 (ratio 1.01). No territorial change of the kingdom is recorded on the Bavaria page between 1816 and 1866; differences from the neighbouring shapes are at the one-or-two-cell level (unverified: page budget).

76,369 km2 against 75,865 km2 (ratio 1.01). No territorial change of the kingdom is recorded on the Bavaria page between 1816 and 1866; differences from the neighbouring shapes are at the one-or-two-cell level (unverified: page budget). The 1836-1839 dip of two cells coincides with Cliopatria's 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha' row (1836-1839) and looks like an overlap artefact.

76,590 km2 against 75,865 km2 (ratio 1.01). No territorial change of the kingdom is recorded on the Bavaria page between 1816 and 1866; differences from the neighbouring shapes are at the one-or-two-cell level (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: the full kingdom including the Rhenish Palatinate (the 1853 shape), with the Palatinate contested in May-June 1849 only

keyframe_review.note: 72,721 km2 (ratio 0.96) and no Palatinate cells for 1849-1852, as if the Palatinate had left Bavaria. The Palatine Uprising page: a provisional government under Reichard was set up on 17 May 1849, Prussian troops intervened from 11 June, 'fighting on Palatine soil was practically over' by 18-19 June, and 'If only for a few weeks, the Rhenish Palatinate achieved separation from Bavarian rule'. The Palatinate stayed Bavarian; the contest is recorded as ledger contest events for May-June 1849.
76,590 km2 (ratio 1.01): the whole kingdom with the Palatinate; no change recorded on the Bavaria page for 1853-1863.
76,729 km2 (ratio 1.01): unchanged kingdom, the reign of Ludwig II begins in 1864.

76,523 km2 (ratio 1.01). The Austro-Prussian War page: Bavaria 'Lost the fringe possessions of Bad Orb and Gersfeld as well as the exclave of Kaulsdorf (Saale) to Prussia'. These are small (each below the 253 km2 grid cell); the shape's one-cell change near the Main/Hesse border (9.05E, 50.11N added; 8.95-8.98E, 49.73-49.97N removed, restored in 1868) is not one of them. Kept as drawn; the three losses are in the ledger.
76,433 km2 (ratio 1.01): the kingdom after the 1866 cessions, still outside the North German Confederation.

correction.text: the full kingdom including the Rhenish Palatinate, as in 1868

keyframe_review.note: 72,632 km2 (ratio 0.96) but, like 1849, no Palatinate cells. No opened page records the Palatinate leaving Bavaria in 1870; the Bavaria page has Ludwig II allying with Prussia in the Franco-Prussian War and the kingdom becoming a federated state of the German Empire in 1871, and the infobox 75,865 km2 sits with the 76,5xx km2 shapes, not the 72,6xx km2 one. Use the 1868 shape.

correction.text: the 1811 shape plus Salzburg: Bavaria after the February 1810 cessions

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1810, which Cliopatria's 1809 shape (1809-1810) covers wrongly. After the 28 February 1810 cession of 'large parts of Southern Tyrol with the Trentino to Italy' and of the eastern Hochpustertal with Lienz to the Illyrian Provinces (Tyrolean page), Bavaria holds Tyrol north of that, Bayreuth and Regensburg (1810) and Salzburg ('Salzburg (1810-1816)', Bavaria page).

correction.text: the kingdom after the Treaty of Munich of 14 April 1816: with the Palatinate, without Tyrol, Vorarlberg and Salzburg

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1816-1819, which Cliopatria's 1815 shape (1815-1819) covers without the Palatinate. The Treaty of Munich (14 April 1816) gives Bavaria the left-bank Palatinate cantons and the right-bank bailiwicks of Hammelburg and Redwitz and takes Salzburg, the Innviertel and Hausruckviertel parts and the Vils bailiwick away; the 1820 shape is that state.

region.text: Augsburg, previously an independent Free Imperial City

ledger.note: 1806: Augsburg loses its independence. 'Augsburg, previously an independent Free Imperial City, was ceded to Bavaria' (Pressburg page, treaty of 26 December 1805); the year 1806 is the first year of the kingdom and Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Altbayern, Franconia, Swabia and Tyrol: the electorate raised to a kingdom

ledger.note: 1806: Maximilian I Joseph proclaims the Kingdom of Bavaria. 'proclaimed himself king on 1 January 1806 as Maximilian I'; 'The 1805 Peace of Pressburg allowed Maximilian to raise Bavaria to the status of a kingdom' (infobox 'Established: 26 December 1806' disagrees). The page names no territory for the core.

region.text: Tyrol and Vorarlberg: 'Napoleon officially handed over the County of Tyrol to Bavaria on 11 February 1806'

ledger.note: 1806: Tyrol passes to Bavaria. 'Napoleon officially handed over the County of Tyrol to Bavaria on 11 February 1806' after the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805: 'Bavaria received Tyrol and Vorarlberg', Pressburg page).

region.text: Tyrol: the rebellion against 'Napoleon's Bavarian allies'

ledger.note: 1809: Tyrol rises against Bavarian rule. The uprising 'broke out with the flight to Innsbruck of young men due conscription' on 12-13 March 1809 and Austria declared war on 9 April (infobox dates the conflict from April 1809).

region.text: parts of the Hausruckviertel and Innviertel (Upper Austria), 'returned to Bavaria in the Treaty of Schönbrunn (1809)'

ledger.note: 1809: the Innviertel and Hausruckviertel come back to Bavaria. The Munich treaty page says they 'had been returned to Bavaria in the Treaty of Schönbrunn (1809)'; the Schönbrunn page dates that treaty 14 October 1809 and has Austria cede Salzburg to Bavaria. The extent of the Innviertel land is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Tyrol after the Fourth Battle of Bergisel

ledger.note: 1809: the Tyrolean rebels are beaten. 'The last rebel troops were defeated at the Fourth Battle of Bergisel on 1 November.'

region.text: the Duchy of Salzburg

ledger.note: 1810: Salzburg joins Bavaria. 'Tyrol (1806-1814) and Salzburg (1810-1816) were temporarily united with Bavaria'; the Schönbrunn page has Austria cede the Duchy of Salzburg to Bavaria in the treaty of 14 October 1809, with France as intermediary. Cliopatria has no Salzburg in any Bavarian shape.

region.text: the Principality of Bayreuth, which 'changed owners in 1810 against a payment of 15 million francs'

ledger.note: 1810: Bayreuth is bought from France. Prussia ceded it 'according to the 1807 Treaty of Tilsit'; 'Napoleon offered it for sale to the newly established Kingdom of Bavaria' (1808); 'it changed owners in 1810'. The extent is the researcher's reading (no Bayreuth place in the gazetteer).

region.text: 'large parts of Southern Tyrol with the Trentino' ceded to Italy

ledger.note: 1810: Bavaria cedes the Trentino. 'On 28 February 1810, Bavaria, under French pressure, ceded large parts of Southern Tyrol with the Trentino to Italy'; the eastern Hochpustertal with Lienz went to the Illyrian Provinces. Counterpart is Cliopatria's 'Italian Republic' row, the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy. Region (reviewer eu-20-g): the Trentino and the part of South Tyrol outside Cliopatria's 1811 Bavarian shape; Brixen stayed Bavarian to 1814.

region.text: Regensburg, formally incorporated on 22 May 1810

ledger.note: 1810: Dalberg gives Regensburg to Bavaria. Infobox 'Ceded to Bavaria: 6 January 1810'; Dalberg 'conceded Regensburg to the Kingdom of Bavaria', which 'formally incorporated the city on 22 May 1810'.

region.text: Tyrol and Vorarlberg, ceded to Austria

ledger.note: 1814: Bavaria gives Tyrol and Vorarlberg back to Austria. 'Treaty of Paris ... in which the Kingdom of Bavaria ceded Tyrol and Vorarlberg to the Austrian Empire' (the page's infobox dates that treaty 30 May 1814, the Würzburg page an Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814). The Tyrolean page: 'all parts of Tyrol were re-united under Austrian rule' after 1814 and the Congress of Vienna. Region (reviewer eu-20-g): only what Bavaria still held of Tyrol and Vorarlberg in 1811-1813; the Trentino and southern Tyrol had gone to Italy and Lienz to the Illyrian Provinces on 28 February 1810 (Tyrolean Rebellion page).

region.text: the territory of the Grand Duchy of Würzburg: Würzburg and Schweinfurt (Cliopatria files it under the 'Principality of Regensberg' row)

ledger.note: 1814: the Grand Duchy of Würzburg goes to Bavaria. 'Under an Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814, he lost his possessions to the Kingdom of Bavaria, and the grand duchy was dissolved.' The Vienna page adds that Bavaria 'gained control ... of parts of the Napoleonic Duchy of Würzburg'.

region.text: Aschaffenburg (Cliopatria files Dalberg's Aschaffenburg land under the 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' row)

ledger.note: 1814: Aschaffenburg to Bavaria. 'Under the same treaty, Bavaria received Aschaffenburg and Würzburg.' The Frankfurt page: Aschaffenburg was the capital of Dalberg's Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, which ended in December 1813; the counterpart is the researcher's reading.

region.text: 'the duchy of Salzburg', with parts of the Hausruckviertel and Innviertel and the bailiwick of Vils

ledger.note: 1816: Bavaria cedes Salzburg. Treaty of Munich, 14 April 1816: Bavaria ceded to Austria 'parts of the Hausruckviertel and Innviertel', the bailiwick of Vils in Tyrol and 'the duchy of Salzburg'. Region (reviewer eu-20-g): Salzburg plus the Innviertel/Hausruckviertel disc of the 1809 gain, minus what stays Bavarian in the 1820 shape (the Treaty of Munich page names 'the parts of the Upper Austrian quarters of Hausruckviertel and Innviertel').

region.text: the left-bank Palatinate: the former French arrondissements of Kaiserslautern, Speyer and Zweibrücken, the cantons of Bergzabern, Landau and Langenkandel, and right-bank Hammelburg and Redwitz

ledger.note: 1816: the Palatinate comes to Bavaria. The Munich treaty page lists the left-bank land Austria ceded 'excluding the cantons of Worms and Pfeddersheim' (the Bavaria page says 'annexed to Bavaria in 1815' and, in the next sentence, 'by the Treaty of Munich': 1815 and 1816 disagree). Hammelburg and Redwitz are already inside Cliopatria's 1814 shape.

region.text: the bailiwicks of Alzenau, Amorbach, Heubach and Miltenberg from Hesse-Darmstadt, part of Wertheim from Baden

ledger.note: 1816-1819: page silent on the transfer. The page says only that 'Austria promised to use its good offices to help Bavaria obtain' these bailiwicks; they appear in Cliopatria's 1820 shape, not the 1815 shape. Year is the treaty year; the real cession date is not on any opened page. Part of Wertheim came from the Grand Duchy of Baden.

region.text: the Rhenish Palatinate

ledger.note: 1849: the Palatinate rises. 'On 17 May 1849, a people's assembly in Kaiserslautern decided to establish a five-man provisional government led by lawyer Joseph Martin Reichard.'

region.text: the Rhenish Palatinate

ledger.note: 1849: Prussian troops end the uprising. Prussian intervention began on 11 June; the revolutionary army retreated into Baden on 18 June and 'fighting on Palatine soil was practically over'. The Palatinate was out of Bavarian rule 'only for a few weeks'.

region.text: the fringe possessions of Bad Orb and Gersfeld and the exclave of Kaulsdorf (Saale)

ledger.note: 1866: Bavaria loses Gersfeld, Bad Orb and Kaulsdorf. 'Lost the fringe possessions of Bad Orb and Gersfeld as well as the exclave of Kaulsdorf (Saale) to Prussia' (no month on the page; the Bavaria page agrees and adds several Lower Franconian districts it does not name).

region.text: the kingdom as it stood in 1870, unchanged to 1918

ledger.note: 12 November 1918: the Anif declaration ends the kingdom. 'On 12 November, he issued the Anif declaration' (Ludwig III 'in no position to lead the government'); 'With this, the 700 year rule of the Wittelsbach dynasty came to an end'; 'the former Kingdom of Bavaria became the People's State of Bavaria'. Infobox: German Revolution 9 November 1918. From 1871 the kingdom was a federated state, 'second in size, power, and wealth only to' Prussia, with its own king, Landtag government, diplomatic body and (in peacetime) army. Was a dissolve in January 1871 into german-empire; moved to 1918 on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (R122). On the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D02) the german-empire dossier dropped its 1871 gain from this kingdom and its identity.predecessors entry, and weimar-republic lists the kingdom as a predecessor (fx-53 D04), so the kingdom keeps its land to November 1918 (the hierarchy.csv row kingdom-of-bavaria -> german-empire, constituent 1871-1918, is for the orchestrator).

wars.name: Tyrolean Rebellion
wars.outcome: The rebels are crushed on 1 November 1809; on 28 February 1810 Bavaria cedes the Trentino and southern Tyrol to Italy and the Hochpustertal to the Illyrian Provinces.
wars.note: Austria declared war on 9 April 1809; Tyrol stays Bavarian until 1814.

wars.name: Palatine Uprising
wars.outcome: Prussian troops put down the uprising between 11 and 19 June 1849; the Palatinate returns to Bavarian rule after a few weeks.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussian victory (Peace of Prague, 23 August 1866); Bavaria loses Gersfeld, Bad Orb and Kaulsdorf to Prussia and stays outside the North German Confederation.
wars.note: The Bavaria page names the war but gives no Bavarian battles; no contest events are recorded for want of a dated page.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Ludwig II allies with Prussia against France; the German Empire is proclaimed on 18 January 1871 and Bavaria becomes a federated state.

certainty.note: Treaty borders throughout (Pressburg 1805, Paris 1810, Paris/Vienna 1814-15, Munich 1816, the 1866 cessions). Exceptions: Tyrol while the 1809 rebellion held it, and the Palatinate for a few weeks in May-June 1849. Exclaves and fringe possessions are below the 253 km2 grid cell.
Frontier unchanged from the 1870 shape (no page gives a change before Coburg joined in 1920); the state is a constituent of the German Empire.

sources.title: Peace of Pressburg (1805)
sources.note: 26 Dec 1805: Bavaria receives Tyrol, Vorarlberg, Augsburg; royal titles; Swabian holdings to Wurttemberg and Baden.

sources.title: Treaty of Schönbrunn
sources.note: 14 Oct 1809: Austria cedes the Duchy of Salzburg to Bavaria. Thin on Bavaria.

sources.title: Tyrolean Rebellion
sources.note: 11 Feb 1806 handover of Tyrol to Bavaria; 1809 rebellion; 28 Feb 1810 partition.

sources.title: Treaty of Munich (1816)
sources.note: 14 April 1816: Bavaria cedes Salzburg, Innviertel parts, Vils; receives the left-bank Palatinate and right-bank bailiwicks.

sources.title: Palatine Uprising
sources.note: May-June 1849 separation of the Palatinate from Bavarian rule.

sources.title: Principality of Regensburg
sources.note: 27 April 1803 creation; 6 Jan / 22 May 1810 cession of Regensburg to Bavaria; Aschaffenburg; Hanau and Fulda.

sources.title: Grand Duchy of Würzburg
sources.note: 1805 Pressburg exchange; 23/30 Sept 1806 Confederation of the Rhine; Schweinfurt 1810; 3 June 1814 transfer to Bavaria.

sources.title: Grand Duchy of Frankfurt
sources.note: 16 Feb 1810 creation from Dalberg's remaining lands; 5,160 km2; Dec 1813 end.

sources.title: German mediatisation
sources.note: Recess of 25 Feb 1803 (Bavaria: Augsburg, Bamberg, Freising, Passau, Wurzburg; Dalberg's Regensburg electorate with Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar); Confederation of the Rhine 1806.

sources.title: Confederation of the Rhine
sources.note: 12 July 1806 founding and member joining dates (Wurzburg 23 Sept, Saxony 11 Dec 1806, Lippe 11 April 1807); dissolved 4 Nov 1813.

sources.title: Principality of Bayreuth
sources.note: Ceded by Prussia 1807 (Tilsit), offered to Bavaria 1808, changed owners 1810.

sources.title: Congress of Vienna
sources.note: Final Act 9 June 1815; Saxony lost 60% to Prussia; Bavaria gained the Palatinate and parts of Wurzburg.

sources.title: Austro-Prussian War
sources.note: 15 June 1866 Prussian invasion of Hanover, Saxony and Hesse-Kassel; Peace of Prague 23 Aug 1866; Bavarian losses.

notes:
END YEAR: the kingdom survived as a federated state of the German Empire to 12 Nov 1918 (Anif declaration); identity.end is 1918/11 since the fx-46 R122 fix of 3 Nov 2026 (it was 1871/1 because Cliopatria's last shape is 1870 and its German Empire row (1871-1919) covers the same land). Rulers are listed to 1886 only. START: the Bavaria page says 'proclaimed himself king on 1 January 1806' but its infobox says 26 December 1806.
CLIOPATRIA ROWS THAT ARE MIS-LABELLED: Cliopatria's 'Principality of Regensberg' 1806-1813 shapes lie on Würzburg, Schweinfurt and Bad Kissingen (the Grand Duchy of Würzburg), and its 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' 1806-1807 shapes lie on Aschaffenburg and Hanau while the 1811-1814 ones are the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt (Frankfurt, Hanau, Fulda, Aschaffenburg). Bavaria's 1814 gains are written against those shapes by name; the eu-20 Würzburg writer and the Regensburg dossier (eu-20-g) record the swap.
SALZBURG: no Bavarian shape contains Salzburg (1 of 26 cells), though the Bavaria page has it Bavarian 1810-1816; keyframe corrections add it for 1810-1815.
PALATINATE: Cliopatria's 1849-1852 and 1870 shapes drop the Palatinate; the Palatine Uprising page makes the separation 'a few weeks' in 1849 and no opened page gives any 1870 loss.
UNVERIFIED (page budget 9, here 13 opened because Bayreuth, mediatisation, Vienna and the Austro-Prussian War are shared with other dossiers): Ansbach in 1806; the 1807 shape's non-Bamberg cells; the Coburg-border two-cell flicker 1820-1840; the Hesse and Baden bailiwicks transferred 1816-1819; the extent of the Innviertel in 1809; the Treaty of Paris date of the Tyrol cession (30 May on the Bavaria page, 3 June on the Würzburg page).
COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: grand-duchy-of-frankfurt (1810-1813, no Cliopatria row of its own), 'Illyrian Provinces' (Hochpustertal, 1810), 'Free Imperial City of Augsburg', 'Provisional Government of the Palatinate' (weeks only, no rebel dossier). GAZETTEER: place Bayreuth, Aschaffenburg, Berchtesgaden; regions Innviertel, Hausruckviertel, Upper/Middle/Lower Franconia are not in the gazetteer; radii are used instead. FX-53 (3 Nov 2026): the german-empire gain and predecessors entry for Bavaria were removed (D02) and weimar-republic lists Bavaria as a predecessor (D04); the 1870 keyframe now runs 'to' 1918, as the kingdom does (identity.end 1918/11 from fx-46 R122).
